options: Microsoft's built-in, subscription-based mechanism for forwarding event logs between Windows machines without a third-party agent
A third-party agent that must be purchased and licensed separately from Windows
A syslog client built into every version of Windows
A tool that only works on Windows Server, never on workstations
questions.explain: WEF ships with Windows itself and uses a subscription model, with nothing extra to install on the source machines.

questions.q: What protocol does Windows Event Forwarding run on top of, and over which ports?
options: WinRM, over TCP 5985 (HTTP) or 5986 (HTTPS)
Syslog, over UDP 514
FTP, over TCP 21
SNMP, over UDP 161
questions.explain: WEF rides on WinRM (Windows Remote Management), using TCP port 5985 for HTTP or 5986 for HTTPS.

questions.q: In a source-initiated (push) WEF subscription, what triggers source computers to start forwarding events?
options: A Group Policy Object pushes the subscription configuration out to the source computers
Each source computer must be manually configured one at a time with no central policy
The collector has no role at all in a push subscription
Source-initiated subscriptions do not exist in WEF
questions.explain: Source-initiated subscriptions use GPO to push configuration to many machines at once, which is the common choice at scale.

questions.q: Where do forwarded events land on the Windows Event Collector?
options: In a dedicated event log called ForwardedEvents
They overwrite the Security log directly
In a plaintext .log file on the desktop
WEF does not store received events anywhere
questions.explain: The ForwardedEvents log is a normal Windows event log specifically for events received via WEF.

questions.q: What is a key tradeoff of using a dedicated forwarding agent (like Winlogbeat) instead of WEF?
options: An agent can forward to almost any SIEM and works cross-platform, but it's one more piece of software to install and maintain on every host
A dedicated agent requires no installation anywhere
WEF can forward to Linux machines natively, while agents cannot
There is no meaningful difference between the two approaches
questions.explain: Dedicated agents trade WEF's zero-extra-software simplicity for broader SIEM compatibility and cross-platform support, at the cost of per-host deployment overhead.
